classes.purpose: Map sources, review reconciliations, and explain exceptions
classes.content: User instructions; the selected Studio Archive client-folder binding, including stable opaque client ID, current opaque scope ID and local paths; engagement, workflow and run identifiers; accounting files or extracted records; mappings; reconciliation results; exception evidence; workpapers and review decisions

security_controls.control: Run artifacts are written to a derived client/engagement/workflow/run path under the user-selected private workspace root rather than inside the client evidence folder or a published repository path.

The raw runner requires a digest-valid v2 Studio Archive client-folder binding with a stable client ID and current folder scope ID, rejects input outside that client root, rejects a workspace inside the evidence folder, derives the output namespace from the stable client ID plus engagement, workflow, and run IDs, and seals the same context into intake, canonical, and assurance records.
The review server binds to loopback and constrains review writes to the selected run folder.

Row-level reconciliation uses only reviewed source roles and qualified source adapters, and enforces current source receipts, entity, party, currency, evidence-reuse, fan-out, and exact allocation-conservation controls before a row can close.

MCP review save and apply operations capture the bounded canonical output tree and modes in parent-process memory, run workflow helpers only against a detached working tree, reject linked, aliased, special, oversized, or unexpected entries, and restore exact trusted bytes and modes on every rejected commit without trusting child-accessible rollback material.

The MCP parent derives the operative run, review payload, current decisions, final artifact state, authorized write set, effects, and readiness from the persisted trusted snapshot; caller copies must match exactly, helper output is acknowledgement-only, and parent replay plus current-byte postconditions must close before commit.

Every assured Python and MCP entry validates the exact 25-file plugin and shared-assurance implementation tree before loading workflow logic; a later review requires the independently retained predecessor checkpoint, replays the archived predecessor rows, allocations and core checks, and rejects missing, wrong or self-resealed predecessor authority without mutating the canonical tree.
